The six-day poll showed 32% of Americans giving a thumbs up to Trump's presidency, unchanged from ​a September Reuters/Ipsos survey that saw the leader's rating at the lowest of his political career.

# Trump approval rating mired at record low: Poll

President Trump maintained his record low approval rating in a new survey released Monday, as Republicans push to ramp up support for their party’s candidates with around four weeks until the midterms.

The Reuters/Ipsos poll found the president’s approval held steady at the 32 percent rating from the polling center’s survey last month.

results.content: A new state-by-state tracker from Civiqs shows Trump with positive net approval ratings in just 11 states, all of which have backed him in the last three presidential elections. The findings add to a growing body of surveys showing Trump's support slipping as voters prepare to decide which party controls Congress.
results.title: Trump underwater in 39 states, new poll shows

results.content:
Figures from Civiqs' rolling tracking poll of registered voters captured as of September 28 show the president is underwater in 39 states and every major battleground state.

Civiqs gives Trump a net approval rating in 10 states: Idaho, Wyoming, Utah, North Dakota, South Dakota, Kansas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Alabama and West Virginia.

Meanwhile, Civiqs puts the president’s overall approval rating at 34 percent.
results.title: Trump’s Approval Rating Hits Record Low Across Both Terms As Midterms Near - Newsweek

results.content:
The figures come from Civiqs' rolling online tracker, based on 133,869 responses from registered voters collected between January 20, 2025, and October 2, 2026.

A Newsweek analysis compares the latest state ratings with those recorded when Trump began his second term, with net approval calculated as approval minus disapproval.

Nationally, 34 percent approve of Trump's job performance, and 60 percent disapprove, giving him a net approval rating of -26.
